title: Stop the claim reader from failing the whole write guard open, and pin the ownership guard's trigger set
action: The sfg-1 judge returned NEEDS_REVISION on two hunt checks. Both are in the claim-derived resolution shipped by commit 9809d34e. FIX 1 (the serious one): store.rs claim_active documents that a claim with no parseable timestamp reads as ACTIVE, never as expired — but it uses `date_parse_ms(claim.get("claimed_at"))?`, and date_parse_ms returns Err(Nd) for a non-RFC3339 string or a numeric timestamp (jspath.rs:448-466). That Nd propagates out of resolve_write_record all the way to hooks/mod.rs:184 emit_undecidable, which exits 0 saying the guard did NOT run. So ONE malformed claimed_at in this session's own claim turns the ENTIRE write guard off, for every path including .bee mutations — a guard that fails OPEN on malformed store data, which is the exact opposite of what its own comment promises. Make claim_active swallow an unparseable claimed_at and read the claim as active, exactly as the comment says, so no Nd can ever escape the claim reader. Audit every other `?` inside claims_dir_g / claim_active / session_claimed_features for the same escape and close each one the same way: a claim the reader cannot understand contributes nothing OR reads as active, but it never decides the guard's fate. FIX 2: checks.rs:534-539 claims in a comment that the msn-21 workspace-ownership check keeps firing for exactly the sessions it fired for before this cell. That is now false and unpinned: `phase` at checks.rs:527 comes from the DERIVED record, so an unbound session whose state.json says idle while its claimed lane says swarming used to reach the isolated-workspace ownership deny and now skips it. Decide the honest answer (the derived phase IS this session's real phase, so the guard SHOULD read it — but then the comment must say so), correct the comment to state what the code does, and pin the behavior with a test that combines a claim-derived record with write_policy isolated. Both fixes are proven red-first: write the failing test, watch it fail, then fix.

truths: A claim carrying a malformed, numeric, or missing claimed_at NEVER makes the write guard report undecidable — the guard still runs and still decides.
Such a claim reads as ACTIVE, exactly as claim_active's own comment promises.

No `?` inside the claim readers can propagate a parse error out of resolve_write_record; a claim the reader cannot understand either contributes nothing or reads as active, and a test proves the whole guard still decides.
The msn-21 ownership-check comment states what the code actually does with a claim-derived phase — no comment asserts an invariance the code does not hold.
A test combines a claim-derived record with write_policy isolated and pins which way the ownership deny goes.

Every truth sfg-1 already proved still holds: bound sessions untouched, no-claim byte-identical, one claim resolves, two features ambiguous, bad lane record falls back, foreign claims ignored, the bind remedy stays conditional.

acceptance: A malformed claim timestamp can no longer switch the write guard off, the ownership-check comment matches the code, both are pinned by tests, and the write_guard suite is green.

trace.outcome: The claim readers are infallible so no malformed claim can fail the write guard open, and the ownership guard's claim-derived trigger set is stated honestly and pinned both ways

report.outcome: The claim readers are infallible so no malformed claim can fail the write guard open, and the ownership guard's claim-derived trigger set is stated honestly and pinned both ways
report.tests: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml write_guard — green (212 passed, 0 failed) — the cell's own verify; store.rs claim readers and checks.rs record resolution are reached only by the write_guard hook, so this filter covers every caller of what changed

checks.evidence: All four readers are infallible by signature and contain zero ?: store.rs:458 claims_dir_g -> PathBuf, store.rs:471 claim_active -> bool, store.rs:488 session_claimed_features -> Vec<String>, checks.rs:104 claim_derived_lane_record -> Option<Map>; the call site at checks.rs:168 no longer carries a ?.

store.rs:476-481 collapses Ok(None) and Err(Nd) into one _ => true arm; sfg3_an_unparseable_claim_stamp_reads_as_active_and_never_stops_the_guard (tests.rs:2334) drives all five shapes to exit 0 and sfg3_an_unparseable_claim_stamp_still_lets_the_guard_refuse (tests.rs:2353) proves the guard still decided with exit 2.

store.rs:518, store.rs:535 and checks.rs:119 all read via read_json_g(..).unwrap_or(None) and fall to continue/None; sfg3_a_claim_the_reader_cannot_understand_never_decides_the_guards_fate (tests.rs:2394) passes for both a garbage-ttl claim and a non-object claim file.
checks.rs:534-551 now says phase comes from the ACTING record and names the trigger-set shift in both directions, matching checks.rs:528-531 and checks.rs:552; the old invariance sentence is gone.

sfg3_the_ownership_guard_reads_the_claim_derived_phase_not_the_default_one (tests.rs:2448) pins both directions at write_policy isolated: idle default + swarming claimed lane exits 0 with no write-policy deny, and swarming default + executing claimed lane exits 2 with the deny.
cargo test --release sfg prints 13 passed, 0 failed and lists all eight sfg1_* tests; the tests.rs hunk in 113093a1 is a pure append at tests.rs:2287, so none were edited.

The three timestamp tests are diff-red: the old date_parse_ms(..)? propagated Err(Nd) through store.rs:525 -> checks.rs:105 -> resolve_write_record -> Outcome::Delegate, which expect_done (tests.rs:80) panics on with the reported message. Recorded honestly: defect B's production change is comment-only, so its pin is a characterization/mutation pin rather than a diff-red test; the builder's reported left:2 right:0 under the described mutation is arithmetically consistent and the test does pin real behavior.
